name: Giorgio Armani
why: Soft, unstructured tailoring — the cut Armani introduced in the 1970s — and clothing around it.
origin: Founded in Milan in 1975 by Giorgio Armani and Sergio Galeotti.
opview: “Elegance is not about being noticed, it's about being remembered.”

onething.n: direct via Neiman Marcus — titled deconstructed blazer on the page itself

notes.wool: the unstructured jacket that changed tailoring
notes.ital: Armani took the structure out of the jacket in 1975 and defined what postwar Milan looked like. The Italianness is proportion and drape, not ornament.

notes.craft: The Armani Group's 2024 sustainability report says its production company GAO runs nine owned production sites in Italy (Settimo Torinese, Mattarello, Matelica, Trissino and others) and also uses outside manufacturers in Italy and abroad, including a supplier network in Asia. Real owned making that does not cover the whole range: a 4.

cities: 12 stores, including Las Vegas, Beverly Hills, Boston · department stores, and its own site

marks: No named fabric or membrane technology, licensed or house, on the Giorgio Armani men's line. The only term-list matches are unnamed generic descriptors: 'technical fabric' (18 PDPs) and 'water-repellent' (11 PDPs). Zero mill, membrane, insulation or branded-fibre marks

craft_evidence.owned_d: Armani Group Sustainability Report 2024 p.13-15: subsidiary G.A. Operations S.p.A. (GAO, 1,275 employees in Italy) 'relies on nine owned production sites in Italy and works with external manufacturers and packagers': Baggiovara (MO), Trissino (VI), Fossò (VE), Mattarello (TN), Settimo Torinese (TO), Matelica (MC), Carrè (VI), Inzago (MI), Vertemate (CO). Production also via 'manufacturers and partners outside the company, in Italy and abroad'; G.A. Operations Hong Kong coordinates an Asian supplier network. Report does not say which categories each plant makes. Owned by the Armani Group (the brand's own group), not an outside parent.
craft_evidence.countries: NC on PDPs. Report: owned plants in Italy; external makers 'in Italy and abroad' incl. an Asian supplier network (coordinated from Hong Kong). No share by country given.
